As an AI language model, I can provide some tips on how you can live sustainably on a tight budget:

1. Buy second-hand items: Purchase second-hand items such as clothes, furniture, and household items instead of new ones. Thrift stores and online marketplaces such as Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist are good options.

2. Avoid single-use items: Reduce single-use items like plastic bags, water bottles, and cutlery by carrying reusable items. You can also make reusable items at home, such as cloth shopping bags, using old clothes or fabric scrap.

3. Watch for sales: Look for sales and discounts on energy-efficient appliances and light bulbs, refillable items, and organic food products. Purchase in bulk, as it saves money and reduces packaging waste.

4. Eat plant-based: Incorporate more plant-based meals into your diet as they are often more affordable than meat products. Purchase seasonal and locally sourced fruits and vegetables to save money and reduce transportation emissions.

5. Conserve energy: Use energy-efficient bulbs, unplug electronics when not in use, and opt for a fan instead of an air conditioner, if possible.

6. Take advantage of public transportation: Using public transportation is one of the most affordable ways to reduce transportation emissions.

Living sustainably does not mean spending more money. There are several affordable ways to live sustainably, and by making some small changes, you can reduce your environmental impact, save money, and promote a healthy planet.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_011_END -->
